newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa JSE turnover up 87 pct year-on-year.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa JSE turnover up 87 pct year-on-year.

text.p: Turnover on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE), excluding arbitrage deals, had surged by 87.3 percent in the 11 months to November 30, compared to the same period last year, JSE statistics show.

Trade worth 106.57 billion rand had been concluded between January and November this year, up from 56.90 billion rand in the 11 month period last year and beating the whole of 1995's turnover of 63.25 billion.
Net foreign purchases on the bourse stood at 4.75 billion rand in the first eleven months of 1996 just off the 4.81 billion purchased in the whole of 1995, the JSE said.
Liquidity until the end of November had improved to 10.3 percent from 7.0 percent in the same months last year.
The market capitalisation of the bourse had risen to 1,132 billion rand in the calender year to November 29 1996, up from 975 billion in the calender year until end-November last year.

The JSE said its overall 100 percent index had in the 11 months to end-November risen 7.8 percent to 6,714, with the all gold 100 percent index 13.4 percent stronger and the industrial 100 percent index up 0.1 percent.
